html:
On 8 August 2023 a wildfire driven by strong winds swept through Lahaina on Maui, killing about 100 people. It was the deadliest wildfire in the United States in more than a century.

Lahaina had been the royal capital of the Kingdom of Hawaii in the early 19th century and later a whaling port. The fire destroyed most of its historic town.

Dry, non-native grasses on abandoned sugar and pineapple land helped the fire spread. Rebuilding raised hard questions about water rights, land sales to outsiders and housing costs, which push Native Hawaiians off the islands. See also climate change.
